confirmed.title: RTS smoother is blind to BSSD pivot handovers: frame re-referencing between prior and posterior snapshots enters the backward pass as a filter innovation
confirmed.description: capturePriorSnapshot runs right after predict() (Application.cpp:1676), BEFORE both detectCycleSlips (:1686) and the update loop; capturePosteriorSnapshot runs after (:1717). Every BSSD pivot handover — the ROUTINE sticky/elevation/disturbance handover executed on the first update pass of each epoch (MeasurementModel.cpp:1450 via BssdMeasurementBuilder::preparePivots), as well as the new slip-phase forced handover (CycleSlipManager.cpp:1204) — therefore fires between x_pred and x_post of the same snapshot. The handover re-references every SD ambiguity, iono and sat-bias state of the constellation by subtracting the new pivot's state value (PivotManager.cpp:391/430/480), while the ambiguity/iono KEYS are unchanged, so collectCommonIndices (Smoother.cpp:114-126) intersects them all and nothing marks a boundary (snap.reset_satellites only carries KF-internal resets; is_discontinuity only complete resets). In the backward recursion x_s(k)=x_post(k)+G(x_s(k+1)-x_pred(k+1)) (Smoother.cpp:226), x_s(k+1) is in the NEW frame and x_pred(k+1) in the OLD frame: every constellation member contributes an identical pseudo-innovation of -x(new_pivot_SD) — typically meters — which leaks through G (near-unity for low-process-noise ambiguities, and through pos/iono/tropo cross-covariances) into every smoothed epoch of the preceding segment. The covariance recursion mixes frames identically (P_s(k+1) new frame vs P_pred(k+1) old frame). Documented finding F1 covers only slip-phase repairs/resets; the routine handover is a nominal-operation event with no slip required, and was explicitly listed in the audit doc's coverage gaps ('BSSD handover ordering', not yet audited). Fix direction: store the per-epoch handover transform (or constellation re-reference offsets) in the snapshot and either apply it to x_pred/P_pred or treat the affected constellation's states as a segment boundary.

confirmed.scenario: Any post-processing PPP-RTK (BSSD) run with run_smoother enabled. Over a multi-hour static or kinematic session each constellation hands its pivot over several times as satellites set or get disturbed; at each handover epoch the smoothed ambiguity/iono/tropo states (and kinematic position) of the ENTIRE preceding segment are shifted by gain-weighted multiples of the new pivot's SD ambiguity value (meters). Static smoothed position is constant by construction, but every other smoothed state and the smoothed covariance are corrupted in fully nominal operation.

confirmed.title: Observation-based BSSD reseeds executed before a same-epoch pivot handover end up off by -dN_pivot*lambda after the handover transform (mixed-frame reseed)
confirmed.description: resetAmbiguityBssdAware seeds a non-pivot SD ambiguity from CURRENT observations: sd_seed = seed(sat) - seed(pivot) (:221-223). When the pivot itself slipped this epoch, seed(pivot) contains the pivot's post-slip carrier, so the fresh value is in the POST-slip frame, while every untouched state in the constellation remains referenced to the pivot's PRE-slip ambiguity. The subsequent handover transform x_i' = x_i - x_newpivot (PivotManager.cpp:391) is pure state-frame algebra: applied to the mixed-frame seed it yields a_sat - a_newpivot - dN_pivot*lambda_pivot, i.e. the reseeded key is wrong by exactly the old pivot's slip after the handover. Affected reseed sites that run BEFORE the handover in detectAndRepair's per-sat loop: the F3 residual mandated resets (:801-812), the F2 LLI full-reset fall-through (:824-830), and the pre-existing unknown-integer full resets — for any satellite in the slipped pivot's constellation, on the slipped band. The handover that then mis-transforms them is either the slip-phase forced handover (:1204-1206, fires when the pivot integer is not confidently known, all_known=false) or the routine disturbance handover in preparePivots the same epoch (triggered by the pivot-variance inflation at :159-169). The deferred_resets queue is immune (re-reset post-handover at :1280-1287, correct frame), and the markAmbiguityPendingReseed branch (:232-241) is accidentally correct because ensureRequiredStates reseeds after preparePivots — confirming the structural fix: route same-epoch reseeds in a pivot-slip constellation through the pending-reseed mechanism instead of seeding immediately.

verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by direct reading. The seed at CycleSlipManager.cpp:221-223 differences current-epoch carriers (StateManager.cpp:1057 uses obs.observed), so a same-epoch pivot slip puts the fresh value in the post-slip frame; the handover transform at PivotManager.cpp:374/391 subtracts the new pivot's STATE value (pre-slip frame) from every same-signal ambiguity with no fresh-reset exclusion, leaving the reseeded key off by -dN_pivot*lambda. Ordering holds: immediate resets at :801-812 and :824-830 precede both the forced handover at :1204-1206 (all_known=false path via :978) and the routine disturbance handover armed at :159-169 and executed in the same epoch's update loop (Application.cpp:1686 before :1693, MeasurementModel.cpp:1450). The deferral machinery (:720-748) covers only culprit-branch signals — LLI sats (:691) and residual mandates (:804) bypass it — while deferred_resets are correctly re-reset post-handover (:1280-1287), confirming the asymmetry; severity 'major' is consistent with the code's own comment (:198-206) that a many-cycle-wrong seed at reset covariance triggers spurious-outlier cascades.

The frame algebra checks out: computeAmbiguitySeed (StateManager.cpp:1050-1090) recovers the ambiguity from the current-epoch carrier, so for a same-epoch pivot slip dN_p the seed at CycleSlipManager.cpp:221-223 is a_S - a_p - dN_p*lambda_p (post-slip frame) while untouched states are a_i - a_p (pre-slip); the handover transform x' = x - n_new_ref (PivotManager.cpp:391) then leaves the reseeded key off by exactly -dN_p*lambda_p (0.94 m for a 4-cycle E6 slip, lambda=0.2344 m). Ordering is confirmed: the immediate reset sites (:801-812 residual mandates, :824-830 LLI/unknown-integer full resets) run before both the forced handover (:1204-1206) and the routine disturbance handover (pivot inflation at :164 trips isPivotDisturbed's P>1e-12 at PivotManager.cpp:253 in the same epoch's preparePivots, MeasurementModel.cpp:1218 before ensureRequiredStates :1221). The code already recognizes this exact hazard for integer repairs (comment :723-730 'applying dN here in the OLD frame would be off by dN_pivot · λ') and defers them, but obs-seeded resets bypass that protection; deferred_resets (:1280-1287) and pending-reseed (:232-241) resolve post-handover in the correct frame, confirming the asymmetry. Severity stays major: the error lands at reset covariance (ambiguity_std default 1e3 m, GnssConfig.cpp:116) so it is self-healing rather than a locked-in bias, but it defeats the SD-aware seed's documented purpose (:199-206) in precisely the common-mode pivot-slip events the machinery was built for.

confirmed.title: Slip-phase forced-handover exclude set is blind to LLI satellites and TurboEdit GF-only culprits — a mid-slip or just-reset satellite can be elected as the new SD anchor
confirmed.description: The exclude set for the forced handover is built ONLY from slips_by_sat (:1195-1198), which contains satellites with MW PAIR slips: LLI entries are filtered out when slips_by_sat is built (:509 'if (sr.sig1.empty() || sr.sig2.empty()) continue;') and TurboEdit GF-only flagged satellites (te.repairs / te.reset_sats, MW silent by definition) never enter it. This violates the block's own invariant comment ('the forced-handover replacement search can never pick another sat that is itself mid-slip', :1189-1194). Consequences when handleDisturbedPivot elects such a sat: (1) An LLI sat whose ambiguities were just obs-reseeded at amb_std^2 becomes the pivot — applyCovarianceReReference adds its amb_std^2 variance to EVERY peer (constellation-wide convergence destruction), and because its seed is post-slip-frame (finding 2) every untouched peer inherits a +dN_oldpivot*lambda value error; the deferred integer repairs applied afterwards (:1224-1278) assume 'the new pivot did not slip on this signal' (:1160-1163) and stay off by that same offset. (2) A TE GF-only-slipped sat becomes the pivot with converged covariance; the GF-only pass that runs AFTER the handover (:1304-1306) then refuses its repair (pivot), resets it (variance inflation), and a second handover fires next preparePivots — double frame bounce. Election is reachable: scorePivotCandidate's variance penalty saturates at -1.0 (PivotManager.cpp:138) so a high-elevation fresh-reset sat beats converged sub-20-degree candidates, phase-signal coverage is a hard tier that outranks variance entirely (PivotManager.cpp:293-296), and handleDisturbedPivot applies no elevation gate at all (PivotManager.cpp:288-301). Fix: union lli_sats, te_culprits_by_sat keys and te.reset_sats into exclude_sats.

confirmed.title: In-place pivot repair's clean-peer pass shifts just-reset LLI satellites by -dN_pivot: confidentlyCleanOnSignal treats a receiver-declared loss of lock as affirmative cleanliness
confirmed.description: An LLI satellite emits only signal-less reset entries, so it never enters slips_by_sat (:509), while its mature MW arcs are deliberately preserved across LLI (MwSlipDetector.cpp:1533-1551) and therefore still appear in all_pairs_by_sat via getActiveArcKeys. confidentlyCleanOnSignal (:930-942) then returns TRUE for it: has_arc_on_sig is true and 'sit == slips_by_sat.end() ... return true; // mature arc on sig and zero slips anywhere'. In the clean-peer pass (:1046-1086) the LLI sat is not in handled_this_sig (it was never deferred), so its just-reseeded ambiguity — already correct in the post-slip in-place frame because the F2 full reset (:824-830) obs-seeded it against the slipped pivot's current carrier — gets an additional repairAmbiguityBssdAware(sat, sig, -dN_pivot) shift (:1055-1058), leaving it wrong by -dN_pivot*lambda at reset covariance. Beyond the numeric double-handling, this contradicts the F2/LLI-authoritative policy the same function just enforced: a satellite whose receiver declared arbitrary loss of integer continuity is treated as 'confidently clean' and given a covariance-preserving integer shift. Documented H4 covers only the inconclusive-culprit-identification variant; this LLI variant is created by today's F2 change interacting with the pre-existing clean-peer pass. Fix: have confidentlyCleanOnSignal consult lli_sats (and reset_sats) and return false for them.

confirmed.title: getEpochCleanPairs affirms cleanliness in the MW-internal SD frame but TurboEdit consumes it as a ZD claim: a peer co-slipping the MW pivot's dN_WL is falsely affirmed clean
confirmed.description: The F1 fix inserts an arc into epoch_clean_pairs_ when |dev| <= 0.3*lambda_WL (:1077-1080). F2/F3 new-code review — clean: LLI sats (lli_sat, CycleSlipManager.cpp:691/696/704) skip both culprit paths and take the full-reset fall-through INCLUDING the sat-wide reinflation block (:861-885) and the TE arc clear (:842); the clear is correctly ordered AFTER turbo_->resolve(), so the epoch's slip-contaminated GF level is dropped rather than rolled. MW EWMA preservation across LLI conforms to its documented observation-domain rationale. Residual-reset loop: a culprit whose repair failed takes resetAmbiguityBssdAware(targeted_key) and is then SKIPPED by the residual loop (its signal is in culprit_signals, a subset of adjudicated) — no double reset; deferred pivot-affected culprits are likewise in adjudicated. Band-attribute spelling mismatch cannot misfire: culprit signals, te.clean_signals, and amb_keys all originate from the same raw_observed signal strings; an amb_key on a sibling attribute (e.g. G01_L2L when the culprit is L2W) is genuinely un-adjudicated (different tracking loop) and its residual reset is the correct conservative action. Combined-IF amb_keys ('L1C_L2W' signal) are un-adjudicated -> residual reset restores pre-TurboEdit behavior (C1 closure confirmed). Double reinflation in one epoch is impossible today (KF-loop helper inert per finding) and would be harmless anyway: reinflateIonosphereVariance / reinflateSatBiasVariancesForSat are assignment-style (zero row/col + set diag) and pivot-guarded (diag==0 -> refuse), hence idempotent.

F4 / (g) — RT arc clearing and snapshot semantics: last_reset_* are cleared at the top of every KalmanFilter::update (KalmanFilter.cpp:606-608) and every outlier-handling pass returns NeedsMeasurementRebuild (:928), so each RT rebuild pass clears exactly that pass's resets; there is no 'Applied with unconsumed resets' hole. The snapshot map is rebuilt by detectLargeMwResets and consumed in the same epoch in both PP and RT (resets always run after detection within processEpoch / the per-epoch loop), matching the rollback design. A second reset of the same arc within one epoch finds its snapshot consumed and falls back to erase — conservative (loses Welford stats, breaks no state). wasCompleteReset branch clears MW+TE for all modeled sats in both paths (parity confirmed). setMaxGapSeconds(1.5*max(gnss_rate,1.0)) at RT construction confirmed (RealTimeEngine.cpp:145-146); PP equivalent in setSampleInterval (CycleSlipManager.cpp:111-118).

F1 gate math for GPS L1/L2 — intrinsically safe (recorded so the finding's band claim is calibrated): a falsely-affirmed +/-1 dN_WL aliases to frac 0.47 -> reset, and |dN_WL|>=2 false-affirmation needs noise >=1.7*lambda_WL (probability ~0). The low-elevation false-DENY rate (P(|dev|>0.3*lambda) ~55% at sigma=0.5 cyc) matches the documented 'reset over wrong repair' trade-off. The mw_clean_pairs key format (sat_sig1_sig2, higher frequency first) matches between MwSlipDetector stats keys and TE arcKey in both consumers (CycleSlipManager.cpp:484, RealTimeEngine.cpp:712-713); epoch_clean_pairs_ is cleared every detection pass (:1278) so no stale affirmations leak.

Magnitude caps (d): TE kMaxSlipCycles=1000 enforced before staging (:356-358); the KF non-pivot detector has its own MAX_SLIP_CYCLES=50 and INT_CYCLE_TOL=0.30 (correct); the MW jump integer and computeCulpritSlipIntegers/deferred in-place 'rel' integers remain uncapped — that is known G4, not re-reported.

Policy conformance (c): no repair site consults isAmbiguityUnresolvable / bias coverage (known H9, not re-reported); GLONASS FDMA peer-shift wavelength issue is known H3a; for own-dN repairs both PP (ppp_utils_.getWavelength(system, signal, sat)) and RT (resolver-carried r.lambda) use per-satellite FDMA-correct wavelengths — consistent. The KF non-pivot detector resets rather than repairs despite holding a consistent integer — conformant with the reset-over-repair preference and its GLONASS-backstop role. Aux detectors reset-on-detection via BSSD-aware resets; their satellite-granular arbitration is known H6.

Reset-sigma survey (h) beyond the filed finding: AmbiguityResolver resolveWlOnly 100 m^2 (known G2 for the missing innovation gate) and NL/WL kAmbResetVarCycles=144 cyc^2 (~2.3 m on L1) are the tightest post-mutation variances — still 2+ orders looser than converged states, so no 'effectively tight' reset exists anywhere; the problem is purely the loose/fragmented/unconfigurable side (filed as minor).

Lower-significance observations (below finding threshold): (1) PP applyTurboEditGfOnlyResolutions and the RT te.reset_sats loop iterate obs->observed, so a slipped signal that dropped out of the KF set at exactly the slip epoch keeps its (stale) ambiguity unreset until re-observation — narrow edge case, identical in both paths. (2) handlePhaseOutlier's pivot keep-frozen branch pushes (sat,sig) to the reset lists without mutating state, causing a spurious (but conservative) MW/TE arc clear for the pivot on that pass. (3) The clean-gate's bia_corrected-agnostic affirmation (ZD pivot arcs, no-BIA arcs) is valid evidence since dev is mean-relative (receiver bias cancels). (4) PivotManager handover-failure reseeds (PivotManager.cpp:691/752) also bypass last_reset_* — benign for arcs (S-transform is observation-domain-invariant) but another instance of the producer-discipline gap in finding 1.

criticGaps.title: LLI telemetry semantics (producer bit-encodings x level-triggered 'lli != 0' consumer) never audited; the prior audit's E3 claim is contradicted by Meas3Decoder
criticGaps.why: MwSlipDetector::hasAnyPhaseLockLoss (src/core/slip/MwSlipDetector.cpp:333-337) treats ANY nonzero LLI as authoritative loss of lock — 'if (!type.empty() && type[0] == 'L' && lli != 0) return true;' — and it is evaluated per epoch (:1319) with full-sat phase resets pushed each time (:1528-1532 uncombined, :1363-1367 combined). But every producer encodes STATE flags, not events: SbfParser.cpp:161 'obs.lli_flags["L" + suffix] = (obsinfo & 0x04) ? 0x2 : 0;' maps the Septentrio half-cycle-ambiguity bit (set continuously until resolved); Meas3Decoder.cpp:272-273 'lli = ((lock < lock_run_[...]) ? 1 : 0) | ((lti3 == 0) ? 2 : 0)' sets 0x2 for the entire young-lock bucket; RtcmMsmDecoder.cpp:477 'if (half_amb[idx]) lli |= 0x2;'; RinexParser stores the raw 0-7 value so RINEX bit 1 (half-cycle possible) and bit 2 (BOC tracking) also trip the gate. A persistent state flag therefore drives the LLI full-reset path EVERY epoch it stays set — and F2/F4 just raised the per-trigger cost (sat-wide reinflation in PP, TE arc clear in both paths), so a sat with an unresolved half-cycle or young lock can be reset-stormed and never converge in the ACTIVE sbf_replay_covl145 config. Additionally, docs/slip_repair_audit_2026-06-10.md:198-200 asserts 'RT therefore has no true loss-of-lock signal' — contradicted by Meas3Decoder's lock-regression bit (0x1), i.e. that documented claim was made without examining the Meas3 path. Targeted pass needed: which SBF block type the covl145 capture carries, lti3 bucket duration, edge- vs level-triggering, and whether the consumer should mask to bit 0.

criticGaps.title: IonoVariabilityMonitor: live slip-adjacent subsystem with zero coverage in either pass and no reset linkage from the slip chain
criticGaps.why: This is a THIRD independent GF implementation (besides TurboEditResolver::computeIvi and the staged GfSlipDetector) — pass 1's IVI findings were about the resolver-internal computeIvi only. The monitor is live in post-processing (constructed when estimation.adaptive_iono_process_noise.enable, Application.cpp:1341-1344; updated per epoch at :1654-1657) and directly modulates per-satellite iono process noise up to max_multiplier (default 100x) via StateManager iono_q_overrides_ (StateManager.cpp:640-651) — the very states the slip machinery reinflates. Its second-order GF differences (update(), IonoVariabilityMonitor.cpp:132-252) absorb a slip as ~3 contaminated TD2 samples that ride the recent (20) and baseline (240) MAD windows, and its resetSatellite (:258) has ZERO call sites — CycleSlipManager::resetSatellite (:76-84) clears only detectors_ + turbo_, and the monitor is not registry-managed. Internals (computeGfMeters sign/units, selectPrimaryPair), slip-epoch interaction with the F2 reinflation block, and its PP-only existence (RT never constructs it — parity dimension) were never examined.

criticGaps.title: AR hold-side lifecycle across slip events unexamined: fix-and-hold pseudo-obs locks (1e-3 m^2) have no slip-release path and previous_dd_wl_ is never pruned and is keyed on the MW pivot
criticGaps.why: Pass 1's AR findings covered resolveWlOnly's float-drag and the missing innovation gate; pass 2 only surveyed reset sigmas. Nobody walked the hold machinery: holdAmbiguities/holdAmbiguitiesDd apply pseudo-observations with hold_variance{ 0.001 } m^2 (AmbiguityResolver.hpp:50), collapsing ambiguity variance ~6 orders below any reset value — after a hold, a sub-threshold slip the MW/TE chain misses is effectively un-absorbable by the KF, and no code path releases a held constraint when a slip is later flagged on that satellite. result.criticAssessment: The two passes plus the documented findings give strong coverage of the slip chain's core: detection math, frames (ZD/SD/DD under BSSD and baseline), repair-vs-reset policy, RT/PP parity of the F4 wiring, and the F1-F3 edits themselves were each examined from at least two angles, and the per-dimension clean-notes are specific enough to trust. This completion pass verified two things the auditors never did: the fixed working tree builds clean (all 18 targets) and the existing 190-test suite passes 189/190 — so the 'fixed tree' premise is mechanically sound. The remaining holes cluster at the audit's boundaries rather than its center. The most consequential is the telemetry boundary: every LLI producer (SBF MeasEpoch, SBF Meas3, RTCM MSM, RINEX) encodes persistent STATE flags that the level-triggered 'lli != 0' consumer re-fires every epoch, F2/F4 just made each firing strictly more destructive (reinflation + TE arc clears), and the prior audit's written claim that 'RT has no true loss-of-lock signal' is factually contradicted by Meas3Decoder's lock-regression bit — this deserves the next targeted pass, against the active covl145 SBF replay specifically. Second tier: two live subsystems with literally zero coverage (IonoVariabilityMonitor, which modulates the same iono states the slip machinery reinflates and is exempt from every reset path; EwlSlipDetector, registry-live and one config token from active), and the AR hold-side lifecycle (1e-3 m^2 fix-and-hold locks with no slip-release, previous_dd_wl_ keyed on the MW pivot and never pruned). Third tier: the ZD (non-BSSD) mode runs the new F2/F3 code under different invariants and was cleared only by extrapolation, and roughly 100 lines of today's diff (max_duration_s feature, replay-config toggles) were outside both passes' scope. None of these undermines the confirmed findings; they bound where 'verified correct' can honestly be claimed.
